title: Preflight chaos canvas + dependency breakout
summary: Preflight tabletop to map failure modes for the upcoming private launch; prioritized dependencies (kafka, kv cache, k8s autoscaler), validated runbooks, and assigned owners for playbook edits, load testing, and SOC docs. Identified two high-risk items: quant-skew on older kernels and stale model routing configs. Decided on a dry-run on staging next Wed and a short focused drills week before canary.
next_steps: Diego to schedule staging dry-run (owners + telemetry) - target 2027-02-17
Maya to own playbook rewrite for KV eviction and fallback - draft by 2027-02-15
Rina to consolidate SOC2/ISO checklist into shared doc and send to compliance - 2027-02-18
action_items: Diego: build a focused failure injection plan for KV cache eviction (due 2027-02-14)
Maya: run quant-skew regression on last-two kernels and report delta (due 2027-02-16)
Anika: update launch checklist to include routing pin matrix and canary thresholds (due 2027-02-12)
Noah: create smoke test that validates model variant fallback end-to-end (due 2027-02-15)
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-10 14:00 PST
Duration: 82 minutes
Attendees: Anika, Diego, Maya, Liam, Rina, Samir, Ellen, Noah

Auto-summary (auto): preflight mapping, two high risk items flagged, dry-run scheduled.

[00:00] Anika: okay let's get started uh thanks everyone for joining on short notice, we'll run through the chaos canvas and then breakout dependencies. goal is to leave with owners and a dry run date.
[00:18] Diego: yeah, quick note i had a late ms - i mean i ran a quick smoke last night and saw some kv cash eviction spikes which is worrying for the long prompt paths.
[00:35] Maya: kv cash? you mean KV cache, right, the prefix cache in the runtime?
[00:40] Diego: yeah sorry, kv cache. so when sequence length passes 4k the eviction churn spikes latency by about 30 to 50 ms in staging, which could push some SLOs.
[00:54] Liam: interesting, is that on the new kernel or the older fallback kernel?
[00:58] Diego: mostly older kernels, the fallback path we use when quantized operators aren't available, but we saw a bit on the compiled path under specific batching patterns.
[01:12] Ellen: is this the same quant-skew we've been tracking, where quantized weights produce slightly different token probs?
[01:18] Maya: yes probably related - quant skew + different kernels can change perf and p95. i put a note in the sheet about that.
[01:25] Anika: okay add that to the high-risk list. i want to walk dependencies first. samir, do you want to call out infra items?
[01:33] Samir: sure. top line: kafka upgrade, k8s autoscaler config, KMS rotation window, and third-party observability retention. kafka consumer group lag under heavy ingress is a big risk for private deployments where customers push bursts.
[01:45] Rina: retention - customers have asked for 1 year telemetry retention for compliance in europe, that's gonna bump costs and we need to confirm plan with finance.
[01:54] Anika: noted. okay charting the canvas - let's list components and failure modes. diego start with runtime, liam on compilation, maya on release, noah on tests.

[02:12] Diego: runtime: KV eviction, prefix cache invalidation race, continuous batching overload when many small requests coalesce, p99 tail on small tokens. failure modes: increased p95, incr token cost, downstream timeouts.
[02:30] Liam: compilation: kernel fallback misselection when seq lengths hit edge cases, quant operator mismatch on newer cu libs, and model routing pointing to older variant.
[02:42] Maya: release: canary criteria too broad, no automated rollback triggers for latency regression, deploy window overlaps with peak in eu sat morning.
[02:53] Noah: tests: no end-to-end smoke for fallback route; unit tests are fine but we don't simulate kv eviction under realistic load.

[03:05] Anika: okay prioritize: 1) KV eviction impact on SLOs 2) quant-skew on fallback kernels 3) model routing stale configs 4) canary rollback triggers 5) observability retention cost.

[03:20] Ellen: quick q - how confident are we in our metric coverage? are the token-level traces instrumented for private deploys?
[03:28] Diego: partial. we ship token-level breadcrumbs in hosted but private had reduced footprints for cost. we need a plan to enable targeted breadcrumbs for dry-run.
[03:37] Rina: i can coordinate a telemetry toggle in the private control plane, we just need the checklist of metrics.

[03:48] Anika: action: diego and rina to agree telemetry toggle set and cost guardrails.

[04:00] [04:00] Liam: i want to call out model routing - last time a config drifted in prod we saw a region route to a bigger model variant that doubled cost. we need routing pin matrix and fallback weightings.
[04:12] Maya: yep i saw that in the rollout doc, the matrix is kinda implicit. we should make it explicit and add a validation step in CI.
[04:21] Anika: will do. noah can you draft the smoke that asserts routing fallback works?
[04:27] Noah: yes, i'll do an e2e smoke that simulates an instance loss and validates the fallback to smaller quantized model.

[04:34] [04:34] Diego: question on oncall - do we have a dedicated launch war room or we'll use standard oncall rotation?
[04:39] Samir: i think war room first 72 hours, with doubled pager coverage. we'll flip to normal rotation after canary passes.
[04:46] Ellen: and who owns the war room? product or infra?
[04:50] Maya: infra for triage, product for customer comms, dev-owners for fixes. we should document escalation paths.

[05:00] Anika: ok breakouts: we'll split into two threads - playbook/runbook fixes and a staging dry-run execution plan. each thread picks owners.

[05:12] [05:12] Playbook thread
[05:15] Diego: i'll take playbook edits for KV eviction and telemetry toggles. first pass by Feb 14.
[05:21] Maya: i'll own quant-skew regression write-up and kernel compatibility notes by Feb 16.
[05:26] Liam: i'll update compilation fallback docs and add validation tests that run on merge. due Feb 15.

[05:34] [05:34] Dry-run thread
[05:36] Noah: i'll draft the dry-run plan with steps: baseline perf capture, failure inject (kv eviction, node kill), verify fallback routing, validate canary rollback. aiming for Wed Feb 17.
[05:49] Rina: i'll coordinate stakeholders and book the window, include compliance and SRE.

[06:00] [06:00] Ellen: for the failure inject, do we have safe knobs to simulate kv eviction without impacting shared staging?
[06:07] Diego: we can use a synthetic workload that writes long sequences to an isolated pool and trigger eviction via VM memory pressure; i'll document the exact steps.
[06:16] Samir: ensure k8s pod disruption budgets are set so we don't bring down critical infra.

[06:24] [06:24] Anika: good call. next area - quant skew risk and fallback correctness.
[06:28] Maya: short story - quantized operators can flip token probabilities producing hallucination style diffs, we observed a 2-4% top-1 change in a small eval earlier. need regression thresholds.
[06:40] Liam: that's why we have rollback triggers based on eval divergence and prompt-level evals. but those triggers are not wired into the deploy pipeline.
[06:50] Anika: we need to wire a check: if eval divergence > 1.5% on core prompts, abort canary.
[06:59] Maya: agree. michael from evals suggested 1% but i think 1.5% is reasonable given noise.
[07:05] [07:05] Diego: side note - telemetry sampling matters: if we don't capture critical prompt traces we won't catch divergence.

[07:14] [07:14] Cross talk
[07:15] Noah: (overlap) also add a smoke that verifies token cost doesn't jump more than 12% under fallback.
[07:21] Samir: (interject) the finance folks set a 15% delta cap for launch, so 12% sounds safe.

[07:29] Anika: ok, let's capture final decisions: dry-run target Feb 17, playbook drafts due Feb 14-16, canary criteria include eval divergence and cost delta, war room for first 72 hours.

[07:45] [07:45] Ellen: any open legal/compliance blockers?
[07:48] Rina: we need a signed data processing addendum for one customer pilot, but it's orthogonal to the deploy; compliance doc consolidation will help.

[07:56] [07:56] Action recap
[07:58] Anika: diego - KV playbook + failure inject plan (due 2/14).
[08:03] Diego: yep.
[08:04] Anika: maya - quant skew regression and eval thresholds (due 2/16).
[08:07] Maya: yes.
[08:08] Anika: liam - fallback validation tests in CI (due 2/15).
[08:11] Liam: on it.
[08:12] Anika: noah - dry-run plan and smoke tests (due 2/15), rina - stakeholder scheduling and SOC checklist (due 2/18).
[08:20] Noah: will do.
[08:21] Rina: noted.

[08:25] [08:25] Quick Q/A
[08:26] Ellen: if we fail the dry-run, do we push launch or have a rollback-only release?
[08:30] Samir: we will push only after mitigations pass; rollback-only is fallback but prefer delay vs risky launch.

[08:35] Anika: ok any final items?
[08:37] Maya: also flagging two upstream deps - a third party caching lib license has a new clause; legal needs to review. i'll ping legal.

[08:44] Anika: cool, thanks everyone. i'll send the notes and updated checklist. meeting adjourned.
